extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems covering multiple math domain categories by modeling operation programs corresponding to word problems in the AQuA dataset.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.citeAs: Amini, A., Gabriel, S., Lin, S., Koncel-Kedziorski, R., Choi, Y., & Hajishirzi, H. (2019). MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms. arXiv:1905.13319v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Using problems in the AQuA dataset and annotating them with formal operation programs using crowdsourcing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Many of the problems are near-duplicates... There are also some problems that are not solvable... Table 2 shows a full breakdown of the AQuA dataset by solvability. We omit high-order polynomials and problems where the solutions are entirely nonnumeric.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We find closely similar problems, replace numeric values with generic numbers, and expand annotations to cover more problems from the AQuA dataset. For similarity, we use Levenshtein distance with a threshold of 4 words in edit distance.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Math problems are first categorized into math domains using term frequencies. These domains are used to prune the search space of possible operations to align with the word problem text. Problems that are unsolvable or duplicates were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators are provided with a problem description, a list of operations related to the problem category, and a list of valid arguments. They iteratively select operations and arguments until the problem is solved. Annotators are provided with math knowledge by hovering over every operation. Valid arguments consist of numbers in the problem, constants in the problem category, and the previous calculations. The platform only accepts programs which include some numbers from the problem, and whose final calculation is very close to the correct numeric solution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Expert evaluation of the annotation procedure for a collection of 500 problems shows that 92% of the annotations are valid. It has 87% agreement between the expert validation and the crowd sourcing validation task. The validation accuracy is 94.64% across categories.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The problem categorization might be noisy due to the use of only one mathematical interpretation for each domain-specific n-gram.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Results are significantly lower than human performance. Limitations include problems needing complicated reasoning, limitations in representation language (e.g., factorization not defined), categorization errors, and incorrect or insufficient problem text. High-order polynomials and nonnumeric solutions are omitted.
